issues.legal_issue: A tenant’s construction supports eviction only when it is likely to cause a substantial diminution in the building’s value or utility.
material_facts: The tenant installed a wooden parchhati in the leased shop to store clothes, with wooden beams resting in holes made in the walls.
The tenant’s expert testified that the structure was temporary, removable, and did not affect the shop’s structural soundness or utility; the landlord produced no contrary expert evidence.
The Rent Controller and Appellate Authority found material impairment, and the High Court affirmed those findings.
issues.conclusion: The parchhati did not establish a ground for eviction because the evidence did not show substantial impairment of the building’s value or utility; the eviction petition was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 13(2)(iii) of the East Punjab Urban Rent Restriction Act, 1949, it is not enough that a tenant’s construction affects or diminishes value or utility: the impairment must be substantial and significant, assessed from the commercial, monetary, or utilitarian perspective. The Court applied the reasoning on material alteration in Om Prakash v. Amar Singh, [1987] 1 SCC 458, and Brijendra Nath Bhargava v. Harsh Wardhan, [1988] 1 SCC 454, and referred to Govindaswamy Naidu v. Pushpalammal, AIR 1952 Mad 181; Smt. Savitri Devi v. U.S. Bajpai, AIR 1956 Nag 60; Charan Singh v. Shrimati Ananthi, [1966] 6 PLR 780; G. Natarajan v. P. Thandavarayan, [1969] RCJ 733; Shri Anup Chand v. Shri Trilok Singh, [1977] 1 RCJ 752; and Gobind Ram v. Smt. Kaushalya Rani, [1983] 1 RCJ 295.

rule.if: rent_eviction_proceeding and tenant_made_construction and temporary_removable_structure and not substantial_impairment_shown

predicates.rent_eviction_proceeding: A landlord sought eviction on the basis of a tenant’s construction in leased premises.
predicates.tenant_made_construction: The tenant made a construction in the leased premises.
predicates.temporary_removable_structure: The construction was temporary and could be removed without materially affecting the building.
predicates.substantial_impairment_shown: Evidence showed that the construction substantially diminished the building’s value or utility.

issues.definition: When eviction is sought because of a tenant’s construction, a temporary and removable structure without evidence of substantial impairment does not establish the eviction ground.

issues.legal_issue: Whether a finding of material impairment by a tenant’s construction is a pure question of fact or a mixed question of fact and law determines whether a reviewing court must apply the correct legal test.
material_facts: The lower authorities found that the parchhati materially impaired the building without a sufficient evidentiary basis, despite the tenant’s expert evidence that it was temporary and did not affect the building’s soundness or utility.
The High Court affirmed the concurrent findings without applying the correct legal test for material impairment.
The tenant appealed from the High Court’s dismissal of the revision against the eviction orders.
issues.conclusion: The High Court erred in affirming the findings without applying the correct legal principles; the Supreme Court set aside the High Court’s order and the eviction orders, and dismissed the eviction petition.
issues.legal_principle: The physical nature of a construction may be a question of fact, but whether it materially impairs the premises is a mixed question of fact and law that must be determined using the correct legal test. The Court relied particularly on Om Prakash v. Amar Singh, [1987] 1 SCC 458, and applied the material-impairment standard under section 13(2)(iii) of the East Punjab Urban Rent Restriction Act, 1949; the appeal arose after revision under section 15(5) of that Act.

predicates.appeal_from_revisional_eviction_order: A party appealed from a reviewing court’s decision affirming eviction orders after a revision proceeding.
predicates.lower_findings_lack_evidentiary_basis: The authorities that first decided the eviction claim found material impairment without an adequate evidentiary basis.
predicates.reviewing_court_did_not_apply_correct_te: The reviewing court affirmed the findings without applying the legal test governing material impairment.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges eviction orders that rest on unsupported findings and the reviewing court failed to apply the governing legal test, the eviction orders are set aside.
